key_insight: A GaOx hole transport layer can be made conductive in 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cells through co-evaporation-driven ion exchange, enabling strong passivation and a record VOC above 550 mV.
engineering_relevance: This shows GaOx can serve as an effective back-contact/passivation layer for high-efficiency tandem-ready chalcopyrite bottom cells without requiring heavy alkali or Ag additions.
method: Formed GaOx during co-evaporation of the low-bandgap CuInSe2 absorber.
Tested whether Cu addition, Na, and oxygen flow during sputtering affect GaOx conductivity.
Examined the structural state of the GaOx layer and optimized it for device performance.
evidence_signal: The optimized device achieved over 16% active-area efficiency and a record-certified open-circuit voltage of 552 mV, indicating effective hole transport and reduced recombination.
watch_item: Conductivity appears tied to the specific formation route and partial crystallinity of GaOx, so performance may be sensitive to process integration and back-contact material choice.
paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
